title: When the Postcards Breaks
premise: Ansel Coldharbour, once a celebrated piano prodigy who abandoned the stage after a family scandal, returns to the Meridian Conservatory as a janitor, cataloguing the silences that broke his family apart. At his mother's funeral, a stranger named Vera Ilves addresses the Coldharbours by their true surname — Vask — a name erased decades ago, and reveals she is the daughter of the woman his father wronged and abandoned. As Ansel and Vera dig through letters, postcards, and an old photograph album, they uncover that Ansel's father stole not only a life but a composition — the postcard suite Ansel has played all his own. Forced to choose between protecting the family name and giving the music back, Ansel performs the restored work publicly as Vera's inheritance, confessing everything; in doing so he forgives her, forgives himself, and finally leaves the conservatory's corridors for good.
about_author: Theo Dunmore is the pen name of a former conservatory caretaker who spent fifteen years sweeping concert halls before writing about them. Their fiction explores the quiet violence of respectable families and the justice people build when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ten years after vanishing from the stage, Ansel mops the Meridian Conservatory floors at dawn, keeping mental lists of everything he never told anyone. A notice of his mother's death arrives pinned to his locker. Emotional beat: numb routine cracked open by grief.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: At the funeral, a composed stranger, Vera Ilves, offers condolences to 'the Vask family.' Ansel's brother Hal goes white; their father's portrait seems to watch. Ansel follows her out but loses her in the rain. Beat: the past arriving with a face.

chapters.title: Postcards from a Burned Address
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. In a rented room, Vera rereads forty years of unsigned postcards her late mother received from someone signing only 'V.' She came to return them — or to be acknowledged. Beat: longing braided with resentment.

chapters.title: The Photograph Album
chapters.summary: Ansel finds a hidden album: his father young, arm around a dark-haired woman at a lakeside — not his mother. On the back, 'E. & L., Vask summer, 1979.' He recognizes the woman's smile on Vera's face. Beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: Hal's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hal's POV. Hal, keeper of the family's respectability, confronts Ansel: whatever Vera wants, pay her off, sign nothing. He reveals fragments — their father ruined a business partner named Liis Vask and took her compositions. Beat: complicity dressed as protection.

chapters.title: The Janitor's Key
chapters.summary: Ansel uses his janitorial keys to enter the archive where his father's papers are sealed. He finds the manuscript of 'Postcard Suite' in two hands — his father's corrections over another composer's original notation. Beat: theft made physical, ink on ink.

chapters.title: What the Lake Kept
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera travels to the lakeside town, finding neighbors who remember Liis Vask playing 'her beautiful sad pieces' before she was institutionalized and died poor. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: First Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Ansel, unable to resist, plays the suite's opening bars alone at night in the empty recital hall — and realizes he has performed stolen music his entire career. Vera appears in the doorway, having followed him. Beat: shame and recognition colliding.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: In a diner, Vera lays out what she wants: public attribution, the estate's acknowledgment of Liis, and the postcards returned to the family record. Ansel agrees to help — against Hal's explicit warning. Beat: alliance formed across old wounds.

chapters.title: The Conservatory Board
chapters.summary: Ansel petitions the conservatory to review the work's provenance; the board, funded by Coldharbour money, stonewalls politely. His old mentor warns him off, then quietly slips him a 1981 program listing 'L. Vask' as composer. Beat: institutions closing ranks.

chapters.title: Letters in the Wall
chapters.summary: Renovations expose letters hidden in the Coldharbour house wall — Liis's letters to Ansel's father, pleading, then furious, then resigned. Ansel reads them aloud to Vera; both weep for different reasons. Beat: the dead given voice.

chapters.title: Hal's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hal offers Vera money and silence, revealing he has known since adolescence and built his life on the lie. Vera refuses; Hal threatens to have Ansel dismissed from the conservatory. Beat: love of family curdling into blackmail.

chapters.title: Dismissal
chapters.summary: Ansel is fired on manufactured grounds — an 'unauthorized archive entry.' Stripped of keys, badge, and routine, he faces the identity question beneath the job: who is he without the institution? Beat: rock bottom, strangely freeing.

chapters.title: The Prodigy Returns
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera discovers recordings of Ansel's legendary youth performances and understands the scale of what the family — and the world — took from him too. She asks him to play again, publicly, as part of the reckoning. Beat: tenderness and audacity.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Working nights in Vera's room, they reconstruct the suite from Liis's originals, the postcards' dates, and Ansel's memory of his father's alterations. Each corrected bar feels like testimony. Beat: collaboration becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The conservatory, fearing scandal, offers a quiet settlement: private acknowledgment, no performance, everyone keeps dignity. Ansel must decide whether dignity without truth is worth anything. Beat: the moral fulcrum.

chapters.title: Hal Breaks
chapters.summary: Hal's POV. Confronted by his own daughter's innocent question about the photograph, Hal collapses into confession — to her, then to Ansel. He withdraws his threats and, haltingly, offers to fund the concert himself. Beat: duty yielding to love.

chapters.title: Program Notes
chapters.summary: Ansel books the recital hall under the suite's true title: 'Postcard Suite by Liis Vask, completed by Ansel Coldharbour-Vask.' Invitations go out; the board threatens legal action; Vera signs her mother's name to the claim. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Intermission
chapters.summary: Hours before the concert, lawyers arrive with an injunction threat; the hall manager wavers. Ansel, in his janitor's uniform still, sits at the piano and simply begins tuning. The crowd fills anyway. Beat: calm inside the storm.

chapters.title: The Postcard Suite
chapters.summary: Climax. Ansel performs the restored work before the conservatory, the board, and a hall of strangers, stopping mid-program to tell the audience whose music it is and what his father did. Silence, then Vera stands first. The applause is not absolution — it is witness. Beat: justice spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Aftermath in C Minor
chapters.summary: Consequences land: the conservatory concedes attribution, the estate settles with Vera, reviews call the concert 'a correction.' Ansel declines reinstatement. He and Vera sort the postcards into an archive bearing both names. Beat: cost accounted, honor imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Everything Said
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. One year later, Ansel teaches piano to children in the lakeside town where Liis once played; Vera visits with the album. At the grave, Ansel finally speaks to his mother — everything unsaid, said. Beat: forgiveness as an ongoing practice, not a verdict.
